financial_checks.claim: Take-home on $110,000: 45% versus 25% gives a "roughly $1,100" monthly difference
financial_checks.result: 20 points of take-home is about $1,430 at $7,150 a month; $1,100 requires about $5,500 a month of take-home.

financial_checks.claim: $620/month truck payment invested at 7% for 30 years is "roughly $750,000"
financial_checks.result: CONTRADICTED for a five-year payment: about $250,000 (monthly compounding; about $230,000 annual); $756,000 needs 30 years of contributions.

financial_checks.claim: Phone: stretching from 2 to 4 years "saves roughly $500 to $600 per year"
financial_checks.result: About $300 a year ($1,200 saved over four years); $600 a year at 7% for 25 years is about $37,900 with annual contributions (about $40,500 at $50 a month), so "roughly $40,000" holds for $600 a year.

financial_checks.claim: Subscriptions: $219 actual versus $86 estimated is a $133 gap; $133 a month at 7% for 25 years is "roughly $107,000"
$282/month impulse purchases at 7% for 30 years is "roughly $320,000"
$6,000 living-room cycle at 7% for 30 years is "about $45,000"; "well over $100,000 spent"
financial_checks.result: $45,700 holds. "$100,000 spent" is wrong as spent (3-4 cycles are $18,000-$24,000) and not supported as an invested value either (three or four cycles spread over 30 years come to roughly $80,000-$90,000).

financial_checks.claim: Maintenance "roughly 2 to 3% of the home's value" ($8,000-$12,000 on $400,000); median home about $434,000
financial_checks.result: Arithmetic holds; the 2-3% rate is above the 1% rule used in sibling videos (rule of thumb, unsourced).

financial_checks.claim: Average new car payment $770; more than one in five over $1,000
financial_checks.result: Experian Q2 2025: $749 average new-vehicle payment (search-result summary); the video may reference a different quarter or source and names none for $770 or the one-in-five share, which was not located.

financial_checks.claim: Millionaire Next Door: millionaires spend about 1% of net worth on a car; Toyota/Honda/Ford brand lists; warranty retailers keep 50% or more; C+R Research $86 versus $219 (stored as "CNR Research"); $282 impulse average; Black Friday anecdote

strengths: Clear list with an echoing frame story and thumbnail-script match.
Strong behavioural tests (broken by function versus by feeling) and restoration alternatives with prices.
Well-placed end CTA with a next-video pointer.
weaknesses: Four headline investment figures are miscalculated (house, truck, phone, "spent").
The frame character is eight-figure then seven-figure wealthy.
The closing "last three items" line dangles.
The promised item-five shock is smaller than the first two items.
contradictions: "The last three items on this list" after seven of seven were delivered.
"Not What You Expect" versus "the first two ... are the obvious ones".
Curtis keeps a 16-year-old truck, yet the $750,000 figure needs a replacement truck every five years.
improvement_opportunities: Recompute the house ($573,000), truck (state the five-year payment or a lifetime replacement cycle), phone ($300 a year) and "spent versus invested" lines and show each on screen.
Pick one wealth level for the frame character and use it at the open and the close.
Move the biggest-cost item to number five, or reword the promise to match its size.
Delete the final "last three items" sentence and keep the single subscribe ask.
